sources.name: Hamilton Public Library
sources.notes: Communico feed, ~2000 events per quarter across all branches. Carries the YWCA immigration tables and employment workshops. Age field is used to filter out children's programming.

sources.name: McMaster Student Success Centre
sources.notes: Custom WordPress card-grid theme, no REST feed. All events render into one page load (no working pagination needed), scraped with a regex parser (kind mcmaster_cards). Long date ranges (e.g. year-round webinar series) are scored on their listed start date.

sources.name: Mohawk College
sources.notes: Drupal Views event-list teaser markup, no REST feed. Scraped with a regex parser (kind mohawk_drupal), paginated via ?page=N. Start/end times come as ISO UTC in the <time datetime> attribute.

sources.name: YMCA Hamilton Immigrant Services
sources.notes: The /new-canada page was program descriptions only; the real events listing lives at /events (found via the site's own nav, 2026-08-16). Open Y Drupal distro - JSON:API is enabled site-wide but the event bundles it exposes (node--event, node--lb_event) don't carry the real listing, only server-rendered Views teaser HTML does (kind ymca_drupal, same family as mohawk_drupal). Mostly youth/newcomer workshops.

sources.name: City of Hamilton events
sources.notes: Festivals and civic events; entered by hand until a feed is confirmed.

sources.name: Hamilton Immigration Partnership Council
sources.notes: Curated one-off events page (currently just the annual Newcomer Day), submitted by partner orgs — no feed, no plugin. Best handled as manual entry, not a scraper target. Re-checked 2026-08-16: confirmed WordPress with no REST events route (/wp-json/ has no tribe namespace), page content is one static hand-typed announcement. No workaround exists; this is a content gap, not an access one.

sources.name: iLink Students
sources.notes: Already the source of several published Hamilton events (Bible study, English conversation groups).

sources.name: Blessings Christian Church
sources.notes: Runs the international student friendship dinners already on the site.

sources.name: Hope Church Hamilton
sources.notes: Sunday service bus route for students already published on the site.

sources.name: Friday Night Prayer Hamilton
sources.notes: Standing weekly worship/prayer night, every Friday 7:30-9:30 PM, 10 Tom St, Hamilton (beside Hamilton Christian Fellowship). No dated feed - Instagram requires login and the Zyro website only lists the recurring schedule, no calendar. Per rule 2 (no recurring events), represent as manual per-week dated drafts if the user wants it on the board, or leave as a recurring program note. Re-checked 2026-08-16: the site's own /special-events page is stale (still showing 2025 dates), confirming no maintained calendar exists anywhere on their web presence. No scraper workaround possible - the real fix is a small generator that stamps out N weekly manual_events entries (every Friday in the build window), not a parser.

sources.name: West Highland Church
sources.notes: The site's own calendar link goes to Planning Center's Church Center product, which is a pure client-side SPA (server response is just an empty JS shell, no embedded data). No public feed without either a headless browser or Planning Center API credentials - out of scope for the stdlib scraper. Needs hand entry. Re-checked 2026-08-16 with a real headless-render: the app itself calls a genuine public API (api.churchcenter.com/calendar/v2/events, full JSON with starts_at/ends_at/name/location) - but it's WAF/CORS-gated to their own bundled app (both fetch and XHR from any other script context get 'Failed to fetch'; direct navigation gets 'HTTP Basic: Access denied'). Confirms the diagnosis: needs either real Planning Center OAuth credentials (the church would have to issue an API app) or a headless-browser render step, neither of which fits this stdlib-only pipeline.

sources.name: Tourism Hamilton
sources.notes: Custom WordPress theme; the 'event' post type isn't REST-exposed at all (missing from /wp-json/wp/v2/types), so no bulk JSON feed. But Yoast's auto-generated /event-sitemap.xml lists every event page, and each page has plain regex-able markup (info__date, info__description, banner__title-content) - found 2026-08-16. kind tourism_hamilton fetches the sitemap then scrapes each page.

sources.name: Hamilton Chamber of Business Events
sources.notes: Not The Events Calendar (that 404s) - it's Event Espresso, whose own REST namespace (wp-json/ee/vX.Y.Z) is public. Datetimes and events are separate resources; parser (kind event_espresso) pulls upcoming /datetimes then batch-joins /events by EVT_ID. No venue field is populated on this site (VNU_ID always 0), so venue defaults to the Chamber itself. Cost defaults to 'Paid' - most Chamber events are member-priced, not free to the public.

sources.name: Invest in Hamilton Events
sources.notes: The Events Calendar REST feed works via ?rest_route= (pretty permalinks are off). Confirmed live with real workshop events.

sources.name: James North Baptist Church
sources.notes: Ascend for Churches (Tithe.ly) platform. The 'Subscribe to Calendar' link (webcal://jamesnorth.church/events.ics -> https://jamesnorth.church/events.ics) is a clean, public, no-auth iCalendar export with already-expanded recurring VEVENTs (DTSTART/DTEND/SUMMARY/DESCRIPTION/LOCATION/URL) - confirmed working 2026-08-16, ~36KB of real dated events. kind ical is a generic stdlib .ics parser, reusable for any future source with a webcal/.ics subscribe link.

sources.name: Mission Baptist Hamilton Events
sources.notes: Custom Django site, static HTML, no repeatable event markup to scrape - as of 2026-08 the page literally says 'programs are on break for the summer, stay tuned for fall' with nothing listed. Content is posted in occasional bursts (e.g. a one-off summer camp seen earlier), not worth a bespoke scraper for. Needs hand entry when something's actually posted. Re-checked 2026-08-16: still the same 'on break, stay tuned for fall' placeholder, nothing to scrape yet.

sources.name: Ticketmaster Hamilton
sources.notes: No public feed, but the Next.js page ships the full event list pre-rendered in __NEXT_DATA__ (initialReduxState.api.queries.cityEvents...data.events), paginated with ?page=N. No price field is exposed, so cost is set to the literal string 'Paid' (an empty string scores as free in build_board.py's scorer - learned the hard way) so ticketed shows don't get a false free-cost credit.
